user_turns: Something I said at an event has caused tension with my boyfriend.

This weekend I (23f) was at an event with my boyfriend (23m), and we got talking to a friend's dad. He recently adopted an indigenous little girl, and they aren't indigenous, so he was asking me for insight on how to include her culture in raising her.

We live in Canada, where indigenous people have not always been treated with respect. We talked about identity, since he wants her to have a connection to her heritage, and about land acknowledgements and truth and reconciliation.

I tried to explain that I grew up without my biological father in a mostly white neighbourhood, and I was often ridiculed and bullied for being indigenous, called a squaw, dirty Indian, dirty. For a long time I was embarrassed of who I was, so now taking pride in who I am is the big "fuck you," because I won't let my heritage be erased.

We've been together four years, and suddenly he's thinking I hate the government and think I'm "owed." He feels I shouldn't hang onto the negative past and that it's not healthy, but I've never been that type of person, I work hard for what I want, hell, I work in a government position.

I'm not stuck in the past, I'm just proud of who I am despite history's role in trying to erase indigenous cultures, and the first part of truth and reconciliation is truth, not letting the past be forgotten. He's still struggling to understand why I'd say it the way I did, but I see nothing wrong with it, except maybe the cursing.

user_turns: My sister and I got into a big argument today about my future son.

First and foremost, please understand that I'm not in the slightest homophobic or against gay rights or anything like that. My sister is lesbian and I had no problem accepting it, and I have several gay friends who I treat no differently from straight friends.
Today my sister and I somehow got onto what would happen if my son turned out to be gay (my wife is 20 weeks along her pregnancy with him!).
I told her I hope he isn't, but that if he were, I'd still accept him the way he is.
My sister BLEW UP and accused me of bigotry, and of "closet rejecting" her lesbianism this whole time.
I tried my best to assure her that's not the case, and that I believe there's nothing wrong with simply hoping your child isn't gay.
I'd just prefer if my son could have a biologic child with a wife, the same way my wife and I are having him.

The way I see it, it's like owning a business and hoping one day my son takes it over. If he didn't, that's fine, I'd love him all the same and he can choose any career he likes, but in my eyes there's nothing wrong with having a preference to begin with.
It's the same as how someone can prefer chocolate ice cream over vanilla, but no harm no foul if their son does not. So I'd prefer my son doesn't grow up to be gay.
Am I the Asshole in this situation?
